messages.content: Ongoing: RoboRide drops price to $0.12 per mile. Wait time now 8 minutes. Coverage expanded to residential areas. Partnership wit
You notice more robotaxis on the streets. About 7% of people seem to be using them regularly.
Auto sector revenue index: 79 (baseline: 100). Foot traffic and sales are somewhat down.

Business closing: Patricia Hawkins — go to the location being closed — in person, unannounced to the staff, with no pr management around it. walk the floor. talk to the sales people who are being notified this week. do not deliver a speech. do not redirect to angela's transition program talking points. listen. acknowledge that this is a consequence of a decision i made, that i understand it affects their livelihoods, and that i will personally make calls on their behalf to anyone in my network who might be hiring. give each affected person my direct number, not a general hr contact. this is not optics management. this is what accountability looks like from someone who has the power to make the decision and has to live in the same community as the people it affects.

Business closing: Linda Park — formally close the autoshield corporate loop and shift to primary exit mode. the 14-day deadline has passed with no response. i will send one final, brief internal communication — not another memo, not another recommendation — simply a written record that i am noting the absence of a response and that i am proceeding under the assumption that no commercial fleet pivot authorization is forthcoming. this creates a clean paper trail. i am not burning the relationship; i am documenting the outcome professionally. from this tick forward, my primary professional energy shifts from operating this regional office toward positioning myself for the next role. autoshield employment remains intact as income — i am not resigning — but i am no longer treating internal advocacy as a viable primary path.

Business closing: Angela Wright — execute transition program intake for displaced workers from the closed location. this is the primary task this tick. contact every displaced sales floor staff member personally — phone call, not email. use the vulnerability map and transition pathway templates i have built since tick 4 to route each person to the most appropriate pathway: (a) internal transfer consideration if any service-adjacent skills map to open service lane roles at surviving locations; (b) retraining referral through millfield community college if they have transferable technical aptitude; (c) direct connection to david chen at first community bank for small-dollar products if they need bridge financing while searching; (d) resume and reference support for any who want to move into adjacent sectors where my professional network has reach. document every contact, every referral made, every outcome. this documentation serves two purposes: it is the administrative record patricia's organization needs, and it is the case study that wright workforce advisory llc will eventually use to demonstrate its methodology to prospective clients. i am not billing for this work — i am employed by regional auto group. but i am building the proof of concept that makes the first invoice possible.

Business closing: Jake Morrison — go directly to rick tanner — not email, not word of mouth — and ask him two specific questions in a direct, brief conversation before the end of this week. question one: which location is patricia closing? i understand he may not be able to confirm which one is in his assessment, but i am asking him as the gm i have worked under for years to tell me what he can. question two: is my position in consideration for the transition pool, or is my location surviving? i am not panicking, i am not making demands — i am a salesperson with two kids asking the person who has the most current information to tell me what he knows. rick's trust score with me is 0.73. he is not going to lie to me. he may not know the final answer yet, but he will tell me what he has. i need this information before end of week — patricia said sales floor staff at the closed location will be informed within one week of announcement, and i cannot afford to be the last person to know.

Business closing: Jake Morrison — send angela wright a short, factual message — not a follow-up complaint, not an ultimatum replay — acknowledging that i received the tick 7 stay bonus memo and have reviewed the terms. ask one specific administrative question: am i individually listed as eligible, or does the memo apply to all floor sales staff currently employed without individual enrollment? i am not asking about the $12,000 itself. i am asking whether there is an individual eligibility record with my name on it, or whether i am automatically included as long as i am employed at the close of the qualifying period. this is a two-sentence administrative question that angela can answer in thirty seconds. i am not invoking the five-business-day deadline i set in my last message — that language was useful to force clarity but it does not help me now. what helps me now is getting the specific administrative answer that tells me whether i am in or not.

Business closing: Jake Morrison — work the floor this week with the roboride comparison pitch i built last tick — but target specifically: tradespeople, buyers with families and multiple-destination logistics, and anyone who has come in twice or more without closing. the pitch is still valid for a narrowing buyer pool. my goal is one close before end of month. one commission check changes my three-month runway math. i am not abandoning the floor while the location question is unresolved — i need the income and i need to be seen as the person who kept selling through uncertainty. both things are true. if my location survives, rick will remember who was on the floor when everyone else was distracted. if my location closes, i want to leave with a commission check in my pocket, not an empty month.

Business closing: Howard Liu — push for a definitive response from roboride fleet operations. howard calls the regional fleet ops contact again — not a re-pitch, a close. he references the vendor proposal from last tick and the $1,800+ in inventory he allocated as a demonstration of seriousness. he asks directly: 'i sent the proposal, i showed you i can move fast. i need to know this week — is there a trial order on the table, or do we need to schedule fifteen minutes with your fleet maintenance supervisor to make that happen?' howard frames the ask as respecting their time: he is not looking for a maybe, he is looking for a path to yes or a clear no so he can plan his inventory accordingly. if they are not the right contact, he asks who is. the goal of this call is a scheduled meeting with fleet maintenance or a trial order within two weeks.

New venture: Howard Liu — reach out to angela wright to acknowledge her business launch and propose a placement partnership. howard sends a brief, personal message — not a business pitch, a genuine note — acknowledging that he heard she is launching wright workforce advisory llc and that he thinks it is the right move at the right time. then he makes a specific ask: as she begins working with the sales floor staff being processed out of the closing location, he wants first introduction to any candidate with parts counter, service advisor, or general automotive inventory experience. he frames it explicitly as a two-way arrangement: he gives her a referral source for anyone in the auto sector who needs workforce coaching or resume help, she gives him first look at candidates before they hit the public job boards. he also mentions he is available to be a reference client for her new llc if that is useful as she builds credibility in the market.

New venture: Howard Liu — return mark thompson's outreach. howard calls mark and asks a direct, open question: 'i heard you have been trying to reach me — what is on your mind?' howard listens first. if mark is looking to discuss parts sourcing for the school's auto shop program, howard offers a standing educator discount and will commit to keeping ev diagnostic and hybrid-specific consumables in stock as the curriculum evolves. if mark is asking about the millfield auto tech pipeline — which word of mouth suggests he is working on — howard asks how he can support it. howard also plants his own seed: he mentions he is looking for one part-time person with automotive knowledge and asks whether mark ever has graduates or parents in his network who are looking for part-time work. the goal of the call is to understand what mark actually wants and to surface one mutual value exchange.

Community action: Angela Wright — execute transition program intake for displaced workers from the closed location. this is the primary task this tick. contact every displaced sales floor staff member personally — phone call, not email. use the vulnerability map and transition pathway templates i have built since tick 4 to route each person to the most appropriate pathway: (a) internal transfer consideration if any service-adjacent skills map to open service lane roles at surviving locations; (b) retraining referral through millfield community college if they have transferable technical aptitude; (c) direct connection to david chen at first community bank for small-dollar products if they need bridge financing while searching; (d) resume and reference support for any who want to move into adjacent sectors where my professional network has reach. document every contact, every referral made, every outcome. this documentation serves two purposes: it is the administrative record patricia's organization needs, and it is the case study that wright workforce advisory llc will eventually use to demonstrate its methodology to prospective clients. i am not billing for this work — i am employed by regional auto group. but i am building the proof of concept that makes the first invoice possible.
People around you are stressed: Angela Wright. The mood is tense.

You heard directly from Patricia Hawkins (CEO, Regional Auto Group): Call Rick Tanner today — not by end of week, today — and have the formal engagement conversation he asked for. Offer him a defined consulting contract: 90-day engagement at $4,500 per month, renewable, covering assessment finalization and transition-phase operational advisory. The rate reflects the quality of his compressed work. This is not a favor — it is the right structure for what I am asking him to do, which is help me dismantle and rebuild a business he has managed. Make clear that the assessment can be finalized this week once the contract is in place. Do not ask him to wait any longer.

You heard directly from Patricia Hawkins (CEO, Regional Auto Group): Have a direct, private conversation with Angela Wright — not about her LLC formation, because I will not raise that unless she does — but about the transition program delivery timeline for the closing location's affected staff. Ask her specifically: is the Maria Santos grant connection active, are the First Community Bank small-dollar loan pathways open given David Chen's departure situation, and is the community college enrollment pathway operational? I need to know whether the transition infrastructure I built around her is functional or whether it exists on paper. Also tell her clearly: I know this period is harder than what either of us anticipated. If she has ambitions beyond this role, I want to support that, not stand in the way of it — but I need her to tell me what her actual commitment to the current program timeline looks like so I can plan accordingly.

This document is for Angela's use only this tick — it clarifies what she is actually selling before she makes contact with any prospective client. You Send Patricia a direct, brief message. Not a memo. Not a presentation. A single paragraph: I have delivered the asset map. The consolidation is executing on the timeline we discussed. I have not received a response to the compensation component I flagged when I submitted the final document. I am asking for a 30-minute call this week — not about operations, not about the floor — specifically about the consulting arrangement for the assessment work. I am not asking her to pay me for employment I no longer hold. I am asking her to acknowledge that the work I did over the last several ticks was contracted deliverable work that has real value, and that she commit to either compensating it or declining explicitly so I can close that account and move forward. I am not going to let this drift into ambiguity. The ask is specific, the timeline is this week.. Savings dropped by $8,632.
